title: A walk still answers differently when the machine is loaded
goal: Scripted walks used to disagree with themselves about one run in three; now it is closer to one in thirty, but it still happens, and always when the machine is busy with something else. A walk that answers differently twice in a row is still worse than no walk, because a real break looks exactly like it. Find out what a press sees in the runs that still miss and close the last of it.
notes:
Follows the press-waits-for-the-panel work (commits 406e7141, 6474d254, 3617e017 on 2026-09-13). That took the four-batch flake from seven failures a sweep to these:

  text-style      6/6, five runs in a row
  style swatch   16/16, five runs in a row
  effects-say-their-reach-walk, 10 of 10 alone
  border effects panel  33/33 five times, then 32/33 on the sixth
  layers           8/8 five times, and one earlier run at 6/8

The two that still miss:

  effects-room-for-the-one-you-opened-walk  step 32 (expect): the control called
    "Twist" in "Border" reads "Border, shut", not "Border, open"
  layers-lazy-rows-walk  step 270 (scrollPanel): nothing called "Background" is
    in the panel to scroll from

Both pass on their own: the twist walk went 8 of 8 and the lazy rows walk 4 of 4
straight after the fixes. Both misses came in the SAME runs where the machine was
saturated, and one of those runs also has align-layers-walk at 185s with "no
done.json", which is a walk that never finished rather than one that failed.

The lead worth following: `settled()` in PlaytestHarness gives a press two seconds
to see its control hold still AND the app go quiet, then presses anyway and writes
"never settled" in the log. Every remaining miss should have that phrase in its
press line. Check first: if it does, the budget is what is short under load, and
the question is whether to raise it or to make a press that never settled fail
loudly instead of landing blind. If it does NOT, the miss is something else and
this is the wrong lead.

Also in scope and cheap: `playtest-all.sh` reports a walk that timed out as
"FAILED no done.json", which reads like a broken walk rather than a hung one.
acceptance: The remaining misses are named: what the app is doing at the moment the press or the read goes wrong, taken from the log rather than guessed
Scripts/playtest-all.sh --no-build border effects panel passes five runs in a row
Scripts/playtest-all.sh --no-build layers passes five runs in a row
A walk that does not finish at all within its timeout is reported as its own kind of failure, not as "no done.json"
